fun_highlights: The vocation fork (soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer/adrift) genuinely produces structurally different lives. Elias Okonkwo going to war at 23, losing someone to it at 38, and carrying that loss into work reads nothing like Tomas Thorne's scholarly arc of teaching cheaply, staying home for dinner, breathing the same air as the dying. These are different shapes, not the same shape recoloured.

The callback system — particularly cb_lookaway, cb_first_loss, cb_books_late, cb_outcast_return — closes genuine arcs across decades. Seeing Beatrix Okonkwo at 47 pass the book that opened everything at age 7 to a child 'saying nothing of why,' or Caleb Castellane stop for a stranger at 50 to pay a debt 27 years overdue, is exactly what this genre should do: the past speaks.

The era layer (war/plague/plenty/hard/turning/settled) meaningfully colours individual openings. Elias Okonkwo's 'These are war years' birth sets up the war-draft at 23 and the war-loss at 38 in a way that reads as one coherent life. The Brandt/Castellane plague-era lines ('A sickness is moving through the country') gate the sickness-tending decision and create a real moral weight that is era-specific.

The dynasty accumulation layer — heirlooms, motto, seat, reputation — does produce genuine cross-generation texture. House Okonkwo's journey from a rented room to 'an old and famous house' over five generations, with 'We earn the bread we eat' crystallizing at generation 3, gives a player something to build toward and feel. The epitaph rotation and theme-blocking (RECENT_CLUSTERS) prevents the same death-note from dominating.

The drifter/adrift arc (y_adrift -> m_adrift/e_adrift) is a real fifth life-shape, not a hole. Calla Okonkwo's arc of deliberate not-choosing — reckoning at 61 with a 'life all the same — wider than most, if harder to name' — reads as a coherent life, not a broken one. The engine's conscious design to gate distinct content for this path is visible and working.

The writing pool depth is genuinely deep in places. The 'marry' card alone has eight distinct framings for ordinary timing plus six for late marriage, plus era/vocation-specific variants (war, plague, soldier, wanderer). The 'have a child' event has eight base lines plus seven late-birth lines. This keeps the most-repeated events from sounding identical.
staleness: The 'guarded character meets someone who wants in' beat (t_guarded: 'someone has gotten close enough to ask the question the walls are up against') fires in at least 8 of 15 dynasties in the transcripts, with nearly identical framing each time: Tomas Thorne at 44, Mira Thorne at 41, Selma Quint at 34, Tobias Aldecott at 30, Greta Aldecott at 41, Ronja Brandt at 37, and others. Because 'guarded' is a common trait and the card has a 10-year cooldown (not once:true), it recurs within lives AND across lives constantly. The prose variations ('Kept the wall exactly where it had always stood' / 'Held the question off one more time') are not distinct enough to mask this.

The 'early gift resurfaces in midlife' beat (cb_talent) fires as a scheduled midlife reckoning in dynasty after dynasty: Ingrid Thorne at 55, Lucan Castellane at 59, Anders Lindqvist (5th gen) at 53, Mateo Lindqvist at 55 (declined), Anders Aldecott 2nd at 59. The question 'did you let it go quiet or did it become the work of your life?' is a single beat with two answers, not varied by who the character is or what their vocation was. The prose for 'You let it go quiet' is nearly identical every time.

The body-decline observation lines flood the second halves of long lives to the point of mechanical predictability. In a single life (say Selma Quint, 82 years) you see: 'The mind has become a room she can close the door of' (age 57), 'Distances she once never thought about have started introducing themselves' (age 78), and still two more body observations in the elder section. Across the 15 dynasties, vit-decline observations appear in virtually every life over 60, and many of the lines recur verbatim: 'The body has begun sending its small bills, and expecting them paid' appears in Annika Brandt (age 70) AND Tobias Aldecott (age 78 description text), and multiple others. The cap of P._obsN < 4 is not preventing staleness because 4 ambient observations in one life is already too many when every life fires them.

The 'dying and what do you want to be remembered for' late-life beat (e_legacy: 'That I was kind' / 'That I built something' / 'That I was here at all') is structurally predictable because it fires reliably in the elder phase of most full lives. The RECENT_CLUSTERS blocking in epitaphFor() works for the death-note, but the e_legacy *choice text* itself ('asked to be remembered as kind') appears verbatim in Caleb Castellane (age 74), Annika Holloway (age 71), and — through the epitaph that echoes it — several others. The choice is the same regardless of whether this is a soldier, scholar, or maker. The vocation-aware framing in the card text is a start, but the outcome lines ('Said they hoped to be remembered as kind') don't track who the person actually was.

The 'a_make_name' reputation-steering card ('be known as learned / hard to cross / open-handed') fires as a scheduled adult beat in an implausibly high proportion of lives: Noor Okonkwo at 32, Henrik Vane at 38, Saoirse Holloway at 44, Greta Aldecott at 35, and others. The prose of 'Set out, deliberately, to be the one no one tried twice' or 'the family came to for answers' is identical each time. Because this is not once:true across the session (only once per life), it becomes a predictable mid-adult signpost the reader recognizes is coming.

The adult-band 'fire that destroys what you built' disaster event (a fire losing house contents) fires in Cassian Thorne at 29, Lucan Castellane at 63, and Anders Lindqvist at 73 — three times across the transcripts with essentially the same outcome text ('begin again from the ash' / 'lost the house and most of what was in it'). With only one outcome choice ('Begin again from the ash' — no alternate path), it reads as a pure entropy event whose structural weight is the same every time it lands.

improvements.what: Make t_guarded once:true at the session level (or at minimum onceDyn:4), and split its current single framing into three genuinely distinct versions gated on age and relationship-type (young/single vs. married with children vs. old and solitary). The current 10-year cooldown within a life is insufficient when the trait is common.
improvements.why: This card appeared in 8+ of 15 dynasties with nearly identical setup text. It is the single most visible repeated beat in the transcripts after the body-decline observations. Making it once-per-life would not harm the 'guarded' arc; it would concentrate the moment rather than diluting it through repetition.

improvements.what: Reduce the per-life ambient observation cap from 4 to 2 (P._obsN < 2), and split the existing body-decline pool into two distinct trigger pools: one for the first clear sign (age 45-65, vit < 45) and one for the real decline (age 65+, vit < 25), with no line eligible for both pools. This prevents 3-4 body observations in a single elder life.
improvements.why: The transcripts show that long lives (70+) consistently accumulate 3-5 ambient observations, several of which are body-decline lines that are structurally identical to each other. The reader's eye learns to skip these. Halving the cap and separating the two stages of physical aging would make each observation land harder.

improvements.what: Give cb_talent at least two distinct forms: one for a life where the vocation DID connect to the early gift (the question becomes about whether the gift was channeled well), and one where the vocation clearly diverged from it (the current 'did you let it go quiet' version). Gate each form on whether P.flags.vocation matches the character of the early talent.
improvements.why: Right now cb_talent fires the same question regardless of whether you're a soldier who had an early artistic gift or a maker who had that same gift and built a career around it. The two lives should face different reflections. The content already tracks vocation extensively elsewhere; applying it here would make midlife reckoning feel earned rather than scheduled.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 more genuinely one-time-per-session (not merely once-per-life) critical beats to replace the most-repeated adult-band signposts. Specifically: a_make_name, the 'public failure' beat (a_public_fall), and the 'body starts its first letter' health scare (m_health) should each have onceDyn:5 or longer. The writing in these is good but the structural predictability of their arrival undermines the prose.
improvements.why: A 10-15 dynasty session (as in the transcripts) will cycle through most once-per-life cards 10-15 times. The beats that matter most — the reputation-steering adult decision, the first health scare — should be rare enough across a session to feel like events rather than curriculum.

improvements.what: For the fire/disaster event (the 'begin again from the ash' branch currently in content.js), add a second choice branch: e.g. 'Leave the ash. Start somewhere new entirely.' — which would gate a wanderer-like arc for the rest of that life, including flagging left_home and removing vocation constraints. Currently it has only one option, making it pure entropy with no player agency.
improvements.why: The fire event's structural function is to reset means and force a restart. But a one-choice event with no player lever is a pure passive beat — the player watches it happen rather than chooses through it. Adding a genuine diverging choice here would make this disaster feel like a character moment rather than a scheduled setback.

verdict: A Life has a strong structural skeleton — the vocation fork, callback system, era layer, and dynasty accumulation are all doing real work, and the best lives in the transcripts (Elias Okonkwo's war arc, Calla's deliberate drift, Beatrix's guarded rise) genuinely feel like different shapes of life. But the variety-seeker will clock the template within two or three dynasties: the guarded-person's-wall beat, the midlife gift-reckoning, the accumulating body observations, and the reputation-steering adult signpost all arrive on a predictable schedule that the prose variety can't fully mask. The game is in the 6-7 range: real strengths that keep you playing, staleness that builds across a session until the player begins anticipating beats rather than being surprised by them.
